title: Permission, Not Possession: Setting Agent Wallet Defaults Before They Harden
description:
The setup: a friend's Telegram channel flags on-chain deployment events on a perps venue; I wired those signals to an agent that executes from my own wallet. Open-source, personal GitHub, open standards.

The trap: approve every trade and the timing edge dies; never ask and the agent holds unbounded power — and prompt injection means I must assume it can be turned against me. The industry's fix is a custodian: the decade-old trade we came here to refuse, back through a side door.

Instead: scoped delegation (ERC-7715/7710, session keys) — spend caps, time bounds, an allowlist, one-tap revoke. A company card with a limit, never the vault key.

Six months of dry-run journals show where the caps would have saved me, where latency genuinely fights safety, and why ~a dozen events is a narrative, not statistics — so it's still not fully live.

The stakes: agent wallet defaults are being set now, and they harden. Permission-not-possession must become the default grant, not the expert path.
